issues.description: Method getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): the UML in problem_statement.md declares the method return type as int, while the starter template's TODO comment and the solution implementation indicate a double return type. Concretely: problem_statement.md shows '+getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): int' (problem_statement.md line 72), the template's Lecture.java contains the TODO hint 'Return type: double for precise calculation' (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 17), and the solution's Lecture.java implements 'public double getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor()' (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 85). This inconsistency between the UML specification and the intended implementation can confuse students about which return type to implement and may lead to mismatches with tests or grading criteria.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across all artifacts. Preferred: update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): double to match the template hint and the solution implementation. Alternatively, if an integer result is intentionally required, change the template TODO and the solution implementation to return int and document the expected rounding/truncation behavior in the problem statement.
